[1/6] Plan: add a literature-based e-consent flow and a privacy-preserving email data-return path for future research articles

impact_assessment.why: The user wants Noesis to collect data for future articles; that requires documented informed consent, a pseudonymous participant code, and a user-triggered way to send the export to the study team's email without adding a server or silent data transmission
impact_assessment.benefits: Opt-in research participation; bilingual EN/TR consent; versioned consent record in the export; email draft + JSON download; no account, no server, no automatic send
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new storage keys, a new consent screen, export schema fields and Settings panel; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: existing local data remains valid, new optional fields
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first storage/UI/export tests, pure email-draft builder, no network code, browser proof of consent + download, full gates
